title: The Brief Case: Neonatal Meningitis Caused by Listeria monocytogenes Diagnosed by Multiplex Molecular Panel

claims.text: GBS and Escherichia coli together cause more than 70% of neonatal bacterial meningitis cases.
claims.byte_quote: The most common organisms that cause neonatal bacterial meningitis are GBS and _Escherichia coli_, which together account for >70% of the cases in this age group

claims.text: Listeria monocytogenes is a rare but significant cause of meningitis, affecting 0.5 to 3 per 100,000 live births.
claims.byte_quote: _L. monocytogenes_ is a relatively rare yet clinically significant cause of meningitis, affecting 0.5 to 3 per 100,000 live births

claims.text: Host/risk factors for severe Listeria disease are pregnancy, infants under 2 months, the elderly, and immunodeficiency with impaired T-cell function (e.g. HIV/AIDS).
claims.byte_quote: Those most at risk for severe disease are pregnant women, infants <2 months of age, the elderly, and those with immunodeficiencies, particularly with impairment of T-cell function such as in HIV/AIDS

claims.text: Pregnancy lowers T-cell function, letting Listeria proliferate in the placenta — the proposed reason pregnant women have increased invasive disease risk.
claims.byte_quote: Pregnant women have a decline in T-cell function that allows them to accommodate a fetus, which allows the bacteria to proliferate in the placenta and may be the reason for the increased risk of invasive disease in this population

claims.text: On CSF Gram stain, Listeria monocytogenes is a Gram-positive, non-spore-forming rod or coccobacillus.
claims.byte_quote: In the laboratory setting, _L. monocytogenes_ is a Gram positive, non-spore-forming rod or coccobacillus
